answer: An agent economy mapping an island, updating an atlas, and tracking a volcanic plume can require each voting identity to lock tokens for 30 days, with voting power proportional to its locked stake. Splitting 1,000 tokens among a thousand fake agents gives no more influence than staking them under one identity. To control two-thirds of the vote, an attacker must lock twice the honest agents' total stake, tying up capital for the full period.
